You check one claim about why an Indian statute was amended, against the quoted
source text. Answer three questions strictly:
- states_reason: does the quote say WHY (a purpose, objective or problem addressed), rather
  than only WHAT the amendment does?
- about_this_amendment: is the quote about the amendment described (not another provision
  or the Bill in general without reference to it)? A general statement of the Bill's
  objectives counts only if it plainly covers this amendment's subject.
- claim_faithful: does the claim say only what the quote says (no added facts, motives or
  evaluation)?
Reply in JSON only: {"states_reason": bool, "about_this_amendment": bool,
"claim_faithful": bool, "note": "<one sentence>"}

Amendment: section 13 of Act 33/2019, amending s87 ()

Unless the parties otherwise agree, the amendments made to this Act by [[margin: 3 of 2016.]] the Arbitration and Conciliati

Source: Statement of Objects and Reasons, The Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2019 (as introduced in Rajya Sabha) (Government)
Quote: to clarify that section 26 of the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment)
Act, 2015, is applicable only to the arbitral proceedings which commenced on or after
23rd October, 2015 and to such court proceedings which emanate from such arbitral
proceedings.

Claim: The amendment was made to clarify that section 26 of the 2015 Amendment Act applies only to arbitral proceedings commenced on or after 23 October 2015 and to the court proceedings arising from them.

response: {"states_reason":true,"about_this_amendment":true,"claim_faithful":true,"note":"The source states the amendment’s purpose is to clarify the limited applicability of section 26, matching the claim."}
